item.title: World Cruise Academy — Home
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Independent, honest guides to the highest-rated shore excursions at the world’s top cruise ports. Save money, skip the crowds, and don’t miss the highlights of your one day ashore.

Why book independently

The cruise line’s onboard excursion desk is convenient — and almost always the most expensive way to book. The exact same tour is routinely 30–50% cheaper when you book it yourself, from thousands of verified reviews. Most independent tours offer free cancellation up to 24 hours ahead, and reputable operators know cruise schedules and guarantee you’re back to the ship on time.

Before you sail

Two things smart cruisers sort out early: travel insurance (missed ports, medical care at sea and cancellations are exactly what it covers) and airport/port transfers (skip the embarkation-day taxi scramble with a fixed-price ride and a driver waiting).

Compare cruise insurance

How it works

Find your port → compare top-rated tours → book direct with free cancellation → enjoy your day and get back on time. Browse our port guides below to start planning.

item.title: Cozumel, Mexico
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Cozumel is one of the busiest cruise ports on Earth, and for good reason: some of the Caribbean’s clearest water and healthiest reefs sit just offshore, and the Riviera Maya’s Mayan ruins are within reach for the day. Ships dock at one of three piers, all a short taxi from town.

Best things to do on your cruise

Snorkeling at Palancar & Colombia reefs. This is the signature Cozumel experience. Part of the world’s second-largest reef system, these sites are calm, shallow and bursting with turtles, rays and tropical fish. Boat snorkel tours typically visit two or three reefs and include gear.

Tulum ruins day trip. The only Mayan ruins perched on a cliff above the Caribbean. It’s a ferry-plus-drive from Cozumel, so book a structured tour that guarantees your return to the ship.

Jeep and beach club combo. Drive the wild eastern coast, then relax at a beach club with lunch and a swim — a great mix of adventure and downtime.

Tips for your port day

  • Cozumel is docked (not tendered), so you step right off.
  • Reef tours in the morning have the calmest water and best visibility.
  • Agree taxi fares before you get in.
  • Bring reef-safe sunscreen for the marine park.

item.title: Nassau, Bahamas
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Nassau is one of the Caribbean’s most-visited ports, sitting right in downtown so you can walk off and explore. But the famous turquoise water, swimming pigs and best beaches are a short boat or taxi ride away, so a pre-booked tour makes the most of a busy port day.

Best things to do on your cruise

Swimming pigs and snorkel tour. The Exumas’ swimming pigs are a bucket-list photo, and day tours combine them with snorkeling and beach time. Premium, but unforgettable.

Blue Lagoon Island beach day. A calm, family-friendly private island with beaches, loungers and optional dolphin encounters — a short ferry from the port.

Catamaran and reef snorkel. Sail out to a shallow reef with gear and drinks included — an easy, well-priced way to get in the water.

Tips for your port day

  • Nassau is docked — town, the straw market and forts are walkable.
  • Book water tours early; afternoon seas can get choppier.
  • Cable Beach and Junkanoo Beach are the closest sand.
  • Arrange beach transfers yourself for less than the ship charges.

item.title: Grand Cayman
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Grand Cayman is a tender port — ships anchor off George Town and shuttle you ashore by boat — so a well-organised tour helps you make every minute count. The island’s calling card is Stingray City, one of the most unique wildlife experiences in the Caribbean.

Best things to do on your cruise

Stingray City sandbar tour. A shallow sandbar in the middle of the sea where you can stand waist-deep beside dozens of friendly southern stingrays. Boat tours include the ride out and a guide; many add a reef snorkel stop.

Starfish Point and snorkel combo. Pair the stingrays with Starfish Point, a calm beach dotted with red starfish, and a coral snorkel — a relaxed half-day on the water.

Seven Mile Beach. One of the Caribbean’s best stretches of sand, an easy taxi from the tender pier for a classic beach day.

Tips for your port day

  • As a tender port, sea conditions occasionally affect access — book flexible tours.
  • Morning sandbar tours are calmest and least crowded.
  • US dollars are accepted everywhere.

item.title: Rome (Civitavecchia), Italy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Here’s the key fact: your ship docks in Civitavecchia, about 90 minutes from Rome. That distance makes a guided transfer tour the smartest — and safest — way to see the Eternal City and be back aboard on time.

Best things to do on your cruise

Rome in a day from the port. A guided tour with round-trip transport that hits the Colosseum, Trevi Fountain, Pantheon and St Peter’s Square in one efficient loop. The stress-free choice for first-timers.

Skip-the-line Vatican and Colosseum. Rome’s two most famous sites have the longest queues. Priority-entry tours can save you two-plus hours — essential when you only have one day.

Small-group highlights tour. Fewer people, more flexibility, and a guide who can adapt to your interests — worth it if you’ve seen Rome before.

Tips for your port day

  • Always choose a tour that guarantees return to the ship for cruise passengers.
  • Wear comfortable shoes and modest dress for the Vatican.
  • Summer is hot and crowded — book morning entry slots.

item.title: Santorini, Greece
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Santorini is spectacular and logistically tricky. It’s a tender port beneath sheer caldera cliffs, and the way up is by cable car, donkey path, or road. A pre-booked tour saves you hours queuing and guarantees you reach the famous villages.

Best things to do on your cruise

Oia and villages tour. Oia’s blue domes and whitewashed lanes are the postcard image of Greece. A guided tour with transport gets you there efficiently and often includes Fira.

Caldera catamaran cruise. Sail the volcanic bay, swim at the hot springs and Red Beach, and enjoy an onboard meal — a wonderful way to avoid the cliff-top crowds.

Wine tasting tour. Santorini’s volcanic-soil wines are unique. Half-day tastings visit cliffside wineries with caldera views.

Tips for your port day

  • The cable car queues badly — a tour or early start is worth it.
  • Ships usually leave before the famous Oia sunset — manage expectations.

item.title: Barcelona, Spain
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Barcelona is a dream cruise port — a world-class city right beside the terminal. The catch is that Gaudí’s masterpieces draw enormous lines. A guided tour with priority entry turns a potentially chaotic day into an easy, unforgettable one.

Best things to do on your cruise

Sagrada Família skip-the-line. Gaudí’s still-unfinished basilica is unlike anything else on Earth, and timed priority entry saves a long wait. Prioritise this one.

Gaudí highlights and Park Güell. Combine the Sagrada Família with the mosaic terraces of Park Güell and Casa Batlló for the full Gaudí story.

Old town and tapas walk. Wander the Gothic Quarter’s medieval lanes and sample Spanish tapas with a local guide.

Tips for your port day

  • The port shuttle drops you near La Rambla; the city is very walkable.
  • Book Sagrada Família entry in advance — it sells out.
  • Watch belongings in crowded tourist zones.

item.title: Kotor, Montenegro
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Kotor is one of the Mediterranean’s most jaw-dropping ports: a fjord-like bay ringed by mountains, with a medieval walled town at the water’s edge. Ships dock right beside the old town, so you can explore on foot — but the panoramic drives above the bay are the highlight.

Best things to do on your cruise

Bay of Kotor panoramic drive. The serpentine road up toward Lovćen delivers postcard views over the entire bay. Guided tours handle the hairpin turns.

Old town walking tour. Kotor’s UNESCO-listed old town is a maze of squares, churches and cats. A local guide brings its Venetian history to life.

Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks. A short drive to the baroque town of Perast, then a boat to the man-made island church in the bay.

Tips for your port day

  • The town walls hike is steep but rewarding — go early.
  • Kotor is compact; no transport needed for the old town.
  • Montenegro uses the euro.

item.title: Juneau, Alaska
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Juneau, Alaska’s capital, is the crown jewel of a Southeast Alaska cruise. Glaciers, whales and helicopter flightseeing all launch from here, and the marquee excursions sell out weeks ahead in summer — so book early.

Best things to do on your cruise

Whale watching and Mendenhall Glacier. The waters near Juneau offer some of the most reliable humpback sightings anywhere, and many tours pair the boat trip with the stunning Mendenhall Glacier. The classic Juneau day.

Helicopter glacier landing. Fly over the Juneau Icefield and set down on a glacier to walk on ancient blue ice — Alaska’s most memorable splurge.

Dog sledding on the ice field. Some helicopter tours land at a summer dog-sled camp where you mush a real team across the snow.

Tips for your port day

  • Book whale watching and helicopter tours well in advance.
  • Dress in layers and bring a waterproof jacket.
  • Many operators offer a whale-sighting guarantee.

item.title: Ketchikan, Alaska
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ketchikan is the first Alaskan port for many northbound cruises, and it punches well above its size. Known as the salmon capital of the world and the gateway to the Misty Fjords, it packs enormous wilderness against a colourful, walkable waterfront.

Best things to do on your cruise

Misty Fjords floatplane tour. The signature experience — soar over sheer granite cliffs, waterfalls and hidden lakes, often landing on the water inside the wilderness.

Totem poles and native culture. Ketchikan has the world’s largest collection of totem poles. Tours to Totem Bight or Saxman Village explain the Tlingit and Haida heritage.

Wildlife and wilderness by zodiac. Small-boat tours search for eagles, seals, bears and salmon runs in the surrounding waters.

Tips for your port day

  • Creek Street, the historic boardwalk, is a lovely free stroll.
  • Ketchikan is one of the rainiest places in North America — pack waterproofs.
  • Floatplane tours are weather-dependent; book early in your visit.

item.title: Skagway, Alaska
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Skagway is a perfectly preserved Gold Rush town at the northern end of Alaska’s Inside Passage. Its boardwalks and saloons are walkable off the ship, but the star climbs into the mountains behind town: the legendary White Pass railway.

Best things to do on your cruise

White Pass and Yukon Route railway. One of the world’s great train rides, climbing nearly 3,000 feet past waterfalls, gorges and the original Gold Rush trail. The essential Skagway excursion.

Yukon and Emerald Lake drive. Cross the pass into Canada’s wild Yukon, taking in Emerald Lake and vast sub-arctic scenery. Often combined with the railway.

Glacier and dog-camp helicopter. Fly to a glacier for ice walking or a summer dog-sled camp — Skagway’s big-ticket adventure.

Tips for your port day

  • Book the railway early; it’s the most popular tour in port.
  • Bring your passport for any tour crossing into the Yukon.
  • The historic downtown is a national park — grab the free walking map.

item.title: Cabo San Lucas, Mexico
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Cabo San Lucas sits at the dramatic tip of the Baja peninsula, where the desert meets the sea. It’s a tender port, and the icons — the El Arco rock arch, Lover’s Beach and playful sea lions — are best seen from the water.

Best things to do on your cruise

El Arco and Lover’s Beach cruise. Glass-bottom and catamaran boats cruise to the famous arch at Land’s End, past sea lion colonies to the beach where the Pacific meets the Sea of Cortez.

Snorkeling at Santa María or Chileno Bay. These protected coves have calm, clear water and abundant fish — the best snorkeling near Cabo.

Sunset sail with open bar. If your ship stays late, a relaxed catamaran sail with drinks and Land’s End views is a memorable finish.

Tips for your port day

  • Tender boats drop you in the marina, walkable to shops and restaurants.
  • The Pacific side has strong currents — swim only where guides advise.
  • Water is calmest in the morning.

item.title: Honolulu, Hawaii
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Honolulu on the island of Oahu is your gateway to Hawaii, and a full port day lets you see far more than Waikiki. From the solemn history of Pearl Harbor to the surf beaches of the North Shore, Oahu delivers a lot in one visit.

Best things to do on your cruise

Pearl Harbor and USS Arizona Memorial. The essential, moving visit — the memorial sits above the sunken battleship. Guided tours handle transport and timed entry, important as walk-up tickets are limited.

Circle island and North Shore tour. Loop the island past Hanauma Bay, the Halona Blowhole, and the legendary big-wave beaches, with stops for photos and shrimp trucks.

Diamond Head and Waikiki tour. Hike the iconic crater for panoramic views over Honolulu, then explore Waikiki — a good half-day option.

Tips for your port day

  • Pearl Harbor entry is timed and popular — book ahead.
  • Oahu is large; a guided tour covers far more than a taxi day.
  • Bring water and sun protection year-round.

item.title: Grand Turk
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Grand Turk is small, sunny and wonderfully low-key. The cruise centre has a beautiful beach right beside the ship, and the island’s reef wall drops away just offshore, making it superb for snorkeling, diving and easy beach days.

Best things to do on your cruise

Reef snorkel and beach break. Boat tours reach the vibrant coral wall for snorkeling, then give you beach time — the best way to see Grand Turk’s marine life.

Island dune-buggy safari. Explore the lighthouse, salt ponds and quiet back roads on a fun self-drive buggy tour.

Stingray encounter cruise. Wade with gentle stingrays on a shallow sandbar — a relaxed, family-friendly experience.

Tips for your port day

  • The beach at the cruise centre is free and excellent.
  • The island is tiny — even short tours cover a lot.
  • Bring cash for local vendors off the pier.

item.title: Mykonos, Greece
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Mykonos is the Greek islands at their most glamorous: whitewashed lanes, iconic windmills, and beach clubs that buzz into the night. Ships usually tender to the old port, from which the town is walkable — but a tour helps you beat the crowds.

Best things to do on your cruise

Mykonos town and windmills walk. Wander Little Venice’s waterfront and the famous hilltop windmills with a guide who knows the maze of lanes and best photo angles.

Delos ancient island trip. A short boat ride to one of Greece’s most important archaeological sites — an entire ancient city and UNESCO treasure.

South-coast beach club day. Spend your day at Paradise or Platis Gialos beach, with loungers, clear water and a lively atmosphere.

Tips for your port day

  • The old town is a deliberate maze — a guide saves time.
  • Delos has almost no shade; bring water and a hat.
  • Mykonos gets windy — secure hats and light items.

item.title: Sitka, Alaska
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Sitka is a quieter, wildlife-rich alternative to Alaska’s busier ports, with a fascinating Russian-American history and a stunning setting on the outer coast. Sea otters, bald eagles and whales are the draw.

Best things to do on your cruise

Wildlife and sea otter quest. Boat tours head into Sitka Sound to find sea otters, whales, seals and eagles against snow-capped peaks — the signature Sitka experience.

Raptor centre and Fortress of the Bear. Visit a rehabilitation centre for injured bald eagles and owls, plus a sanctuary for rescued brown bears — close encounters you won’t get in the wild.

Sea kayaking in the sound. Paddle the calm, protected waters among islands and wildlife with a guide — peaceful and active.

Tips for your port day

  • Sitka is sometimes a tender port; allow buffer time.
  • The town’s Russian heritage is walkable and worthwhile.
  • Wildlife tours run rain or shine — bring waterproof layers.

item.title: Ensenada, Mexico
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Ensenada is Baja California’s laid-back wine-country port, a common stop on Mexican Riviera and repositioning cruises. Ships dock within walking distance of town, and the region blends dramatic coastline with Mexico’s best vineyards.

Best things to do on your cruise

La Bufadora blowhole. One of the largest marine blowholes in the world shoots seawater dozens of feet into the air. The classic Ensenada excursion, usually paired with a lively craft market.

Valle de Guadalupe wine tasting. Mexico’s premier wine region is a short drive inland, with tastings at scenic wineries. A relaxed, grown-up port day.

City and tequila-sampling tour. Explore Ensenada’s waterfront, historic sites and a tequila or margarita tasting with a local guide.

Tips for your port day

  • La Bufadora and the wine valley need transport — a tour is easiest.
  • Bring cash for the market stalls near La Bufadora.
  • Foodies should prioritise Valle de Guadalupe.
